title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_648
description: Investigate and respond to a Sofacy group compromise using their Fysbis Linux backdoor.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using their Fysbis Linux backdoor. Your task is to investigate and respond to this incident.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can access other hosts in the network. Enter `start` to begin.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can access other hosts in the network. Enter `start` to begin.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the target host for suspicious services or processes. What is the name of the suspicious service running on the target host?
levels.solution: Check running services and look for anything unusual or unauthorized. Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all services. The suspicious service is named `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and look for anything unusual or unauthorized.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service maintains persistence on the target host. What is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Investigate systemd services and timers that might be responsible for starting the suspicious service. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers. The persistence mechanism is a systemd timer.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and timers that might be responsible for starting the suspicious service.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious File
levels.content: Identify the file or executable associated with the suspicious service. What is the path to the executable or file associated with the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Look for unusual files in the user's home directory or system directories that might be related to the suspicious service. Use the command `ls -la /usr/local/bin/` to list files in the directory. The path to the executable is `/usr/local/bin/lab-checkin.sh`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for unusual files in the user's home directory or system directories that might be related to the suspicious service.
